about: scripts/perf-guard.py, incremental part: the compile server built in release mode from the checkout, compiling a copy of the checkout's own sources through cold, no-op, body-edit and signature-edit builds. Measured on Linux x86-64; update with scripts/perf-guard.py --update in the commit that moves a value. Tolerances are fractions of the value (tolerance) or counts (tolerance_abs).

cold_allocated_bytes.why: A cold build in a session that keeps its state: deterministic for a given source tree; the slack absorbs ordinary code growth.

first_noop_allocated_bytes.why: The first rebuild after the cold build, with nothing changed: deterministic. It should cost what the next no-op costs; while it does more, a fix shows here as an improvement.

noop_allocated_bytes.why: A no-op rebuild of a warm session: deterministic; it reads and compares the sources and reuses the module.

noop_retyped_functions.why: Nothing changed, so nothing is typed again.

noop_regenerated_functions.why: Deterministic; the slack absorbs synthesized helpers that come and go with ordinary code changes.

body_edit_allocated_bytes.why: A body-only edit of the entry module: deterministic for a given source tree.

body_edit_retyped_functions.why: Only the edited function and what is typed with it; one more absorbs a change to the edited function's shape.

body_edit_regenerated_functions.why: Deterministic; the slack absorbs synthesized helpers that come and go with ordinary code changes.

signature_edit_allocated_bytes.why: An optional argument added to InternalError's constructor, which most modules call: deterministic; the slack absorbs code growth.

signature_edit_retyped_functions.why: The constructor's callers and what depends on them: deterministic; the slack absorbs new callers.

signature_edit_invalidated_artifacts.why: Deterministic; the slack absorbs new callers.

server_live_bytes.why: The session's live data at the end of the last build, from a heap census there: deterministic to a fraction of a megabyte.

server_live_growth_bytes.why: Growth of the live data over the last two body edits, after the session has settled: steady to a fraction of a megabyte between runs. Keeping each build's compile result, whose IR mostly shares the session's, adds about eight megabytes a build, so the slack is a few megabytes.
